faqs.q: Which appliances actually need a dedicated circuit?
faqs.a: Anything that pulls serious power or that you can't afford to lose. Sump pumps, refrigerators, microwaves, dishwashers, space heaters, window AC units, garage tools, and medical equipment are the big ones. Most appliance manufacturers spell it out in the manual.

faqs.q: Why does my breaker trip when I run the space heater?
faqs.a: A space heater can pull 12 to 15 amps by itself, which is most of a standard circuit. Add a TV or a few lights on the same line and the breaker does its job and shuts things down. A dedicated circuit gives the heater its own lane.

faqs.q: Can my panel handle another circuit?
faqs.a: Usually yes, but we check first. Every visit starts with a free look at your panel. If it's full, outdated, or one of the old Federal Pacific units common in North Shore homes, we'll show you photos and walk you through options before running anything new.

faqs.q: How long does it take to add a dedicated circuit?
faqs.a: Most are done in one visit, often a few hours. Longer runs through finished walls take more time, and we'll tell you up front if yours will.

faqs.q: Is a tripping breaker actually dangerous?
faqs.a: The trip itself is the breaker protecting you. The concern is what's behind it: a circuit running near its limit gets warm, and repeated overloads wear on wiring and connections. If it trips regularly, it's worth a look.

faqs.q: What does the Illinois smoke detector law require now?
faqs.a: If your home relies on battery-powered smoke detectors, Illinois now requires 10-year sealed-battery units when they're replaced. Homes with hardwired detectors need to keep them hardwired. We'll tell you plainly which rule applies to your house and what it takes to comply.

faqs.q: Where do smoke and CO detectors actually belong?
faqs.a: Smoke detectors go in every bedroom, in the hallway outside sleeping areas, and on every level including the basement. Illinois requires a CO detector within 15 feet of every sleeping room in homes with gas appliances or an attached garage. We map it out room by room during the estimate.

faqs.q: Why do interconnected alarms matter?
faqs.a: When alarms are wired together, smoke in the basement sets off the alarm in your bedroom too. In a two- or three-story house, that head start matters. If your home was built before interconnection was standard, we can wire it in.

faqs.q: My detector chirps even with a fresh battery. What gives?
faqs.a: Usually the unit itself has reached end of life, and the chirp is its way of retiring. Sometimes it's a loose connection or a wiring issue on hardwired units. Either way, it's a quick diagnosis for us and an easy fix.

faqs.q: Can you add a hardwired detector where there's no wiring at all?
faqs.a: Yes. Running new detector wiring through finished walls and ceilings is routine work for us, and we do it cleanly. That's most of what separates an electrician's install from a hardware-store swap.
